summary.text: Colin Allred is a former NFL linebacker and civil rights attorney who represented the old Texas 32nd District as a Democrat from 2019 to 2025. He left the House to run for U.S. Senate in 2024, losing to Ted Cruz, then re-filed in 2026 for the redrawn 33rd District after ending a second Senate campaign. He defeated incumbent Rep. Julie Johnson in the May 26, 2026 Democratic runoff.

paragraphs.text: Colin Allred was born April 15, 1983, in Dallas, Texas, and was raised by his mother, a public school teacher. He graduated from Hillcrest High School in Dallas.
He earned a bachelor's degree from Baylor University in 2005, where he played linebacker on the football team.

Allred signed with the Tennessee Titans as an undrafted free agent in 2006 and played linebacker in the NFL, for five seasons according to his campaign website, until a neck injury in 2010 ended his career.
He then earned a J.D. from the University of California, Berkeley School of Law in 2014.

After law school, Allred worked for Battleground Texas as Dallas-Fort Worth regional director of voter protection, served as a special assistant in the Obama administration's Department of Housing and Urban Development, and later worked as a civil rights and voting-rights litigator at the law firm Perkins Coie.

He won the Democratic nomination in 2018 and defeated Republican incumbent Pete Sessions in the general election for the 32nd District, then was re-elected in 2020 and 2022, serving from January 3, 2019, to January 3, 2025.
In Congress, Allred served on the Foreign Affairs and Transportation and Infrastructure committees, and on Veterans' Affairs in the 116th and 117th Congresses, according to Ballotpedia.
He ran for U.S. Senate in 2024 rather than seeking re-election, winning the Democratic nomination and losing the general election to Ted Cruz, 53.1% to 44.6%.

Allred announced a 2026 Senate campaign in July 2025 and ended it in December 2025 to run for the 33rd District. He won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 45.5% and the May 26 runoff over Rep. Julie Johnson, 54.0% to 46.0%.
